title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Page 27 opens §4, 'Site de De Rham'. Here Grothendieck sets up what is now called the crystalline site.

Setting: a morphism of schemes f: X → S.

Objects of the 'De Rham site' (X/S)_DR = DR(X/S) are systems (U, U', i, π):
- U is a Zariski open of X;
- U' is an S-prescheme;
- i: U → U' is a nilpotent S-immersion;
- π is a divided-power structure on the ideal J = ker(O_{U'} → O_U).

The page adds a qualifier on the PD structure ('tranquilles?/triangulaires?'), followed by 'pas en général'. This connects to the previous page, which introduces nil-triangular or nilpotent divided powers (x^{(i)} = 0 for i ≥ n) together with exp/log isomorphisms 1+J ≅ J. The qualifier is therefore presumably a PD-nilpotence condition, which he says is not to be imposed in general.

An earlier crossed-out version used quadruples (U, A, φ, π*): a sheaf of rings A on U with a PD ideal, i.e. a ringed-space formulation. It was replaced by the thickening formulation.

Remaining structure on the page:
- Morphisms are the evident ones.
- The topology is the Zariski topology, i.e. covers are Zariski covers of U'.
- He defines a restricted, or 'strict', De Rham site DR_st(X/S). It is the full subcategory of objects for which, locally on U', there exists a retraction U' → U. The retraction is explicitly not part of the data.
- The associated topoi are named, with the convention of dropping '/S' when no ambiguity arises.
- The next page gives the diagram Zar → DR_strat → Strat over DR → Cris. Here 'Cris' must denote the PD-free nilpotent-thickening (infinitesimal) site.

Purpose: to set up the site whose cohomology of O computes de Rham cohomology. The strict site is designed so that the object X̃ (X with its locally retracting thickenings) covers the final object, which allows a Čech–Leray spectral sequence via the PD-envelopes of diagonals X̃^{ν+1}. This matches the comparison 'crystalline cohomology = de Rham cohomology' strategy of Grothendieck's 1966 IHES lectures 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés), developed by Berthelot.

Correctness of the next page's claims:
- If X is formally smooth, every object locally admits a retraction. J is nil, so formal smoothness lifts the identity of U locally on affine U'. Hence DR_strat = DR, and the vertical arrows are equivalences.
- In characteristic 0, PD structures on an ideal are unique and always exist. Hence the horizontal arrows DR → Cris and DR_strat → Strat are equivalences.
errors: No mathematical error on this page itself; the definition is a draft. The PD-compatibility conditions are left unstated: compatibility with a PD structure on S (or on the base ideal), and the requirement that morphisms be PD-morphisms. Berthelot later made these essential.

The qualifier on π is illegible ('tranquilles?'). Whether a PD-nilpotence condition is intended is ambiguous. Berthelot's final theory does not impose PD-nilpotence in general, consistent with '(pas en général)'.

ideas.what: Site whose objects are PD-thickenings (U ⊂ X open, nilpotent immersion U → U', PD structure on the ideal), with Zariski topology; called 'site de De Rham'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1966 IHES lectures), developed by Berthelot (thesis 1972, LNM 407, 1974)
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, in Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas (1968)

ideas.what: Restricted/strict site: objects that locally on U' admit a retraction onto U, the retraction not being part of the data; it agrees with the full site when X is formally smooth
ideas.modern_name: restricted crystalline/infinitesimal site (objects locally retracting), used to compute cohomology by Čech methods via PD-envelopes of diagonals
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (restricted infinitesimal site in Dix exposés); Berthelot
ideas.where_published: Possibly in Dix exposés (restricted infinitesimal site); unsure of exact form

ideas.what: Abandoned ringed-space formulation (U, A, φ, π*), replaced by thickenings U → U'
ideas.modern_name: PD-ringed-space versus thickening description of crystalline site

missed.claim: Historical naming detail: the crystalline site was first called the 'site de De Rham' (DR(X/S)), while 'Cris' was reserved for the PD-free infinitesimal (nilpotent-thickening) site. This is the reverse of later usage.
missed.quote: Les objets du site de De Rham (X/S)_DR, ou DR(X/S), sont les systèmes (U, U', i, π)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of historical interest: it documents the terminology shift before the 1966 lectures fixed 'cristallin' for the PD version.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an early draft of the standard definition of the crystalline site plus a restricted variant. Both are in Grothendieck's 1966 lectures and Berthelot's work. Only the naming inversion is mildly notable.
transcription_corrections: The qualifier after 'puissances divisées' is uncertain: possibly 'nil-triangulaires' or 'nilpotentes', echoing the previous page, rather than 'tranquilles'.
The crossed-out quadruple reads approximately (U, A, φ, π*). The struck line after 'ouvert de X' reads 'A un faisceau ... i: U → U'' and was replaced.
The marginal diagram is U' ← U ⊂ X with f: X → S below; the arrow U → U' is the immersion i.
